justification: Both surfaces show the same distinctive scheme: bearded, profile-facing figures in low relief with layered feathered wings, tightly curled hair and beard, fringed and rosette-studded garments, and an arm extended to hold a small object (a rosette/disc appears in A, a cup-like item in B), all set in a horizontal wall register. A is a close-up of a single winged figure's torso and wings, so the multi-figure interaction visible in B (facing pairs across a panel joint) cannot be fully matched, which is the main difference in depicted content rather than in tradition.
